$comment: What the SDK schema cannot say about the Swift side of each generated CmuxNextDaemon request type (swift_app/emit.py explains the rules). A family is one Requests/<Family> folder; it moves here from hand-written Swift in one change.

feed-local-handoff-abort.name: FeedLocalHandoffAbortRequest
doc: `feed-local-handoff-abort {item}` (the verified app connection only): the
cloud owner answered `feed.adopt.cancel` with `cancelled: true`, so the
item is open here again. Never on a timeout or a lost reply.

feed-local-handoff-done.name: FeedLocalHandoffDoneRequest
doc: `feed-local-handoff-done {item, home}` (the verified app connection only):
the new owner committed the item; it becomes `moved`.

list-bookmarks.name: ListBookmarksRequest
doc: `list-bookmarks`: one profile's nodes, ordered by parent then index.

create-bookmark.name: CreateBookmarkRequest
doc: `create-bookmark`: an existing `bookmark` id returns the stored node.
The exactly-once key; reuse it on every retry of this write.

update-bookmark.name: UpdateBookmarkRequest
doc: `update-bookmark`: absent keeps; `.clear` sends null. `icon`
(`bookmark-icon-v1`) is for folders only: the daemon refuses it, null
included, on a URL bookmark, and an asset icon must already be stored there.

move-bookmark.name: MoveBookmarkRequest
doc: `move-bookmark`: `index` is the final position among the new siblings.

delete-bookmark.name: DeleteBookmarkRequest
doc: `delete-bookmark`: removes the node and its subtree.

import-bookmarks.name: ImportBookmarksRequest
doc: `import-bookmarks`: one transaction. With `sourceKey` and `replace`, the
folder carrying `sourceKey` keeps its id and position and takes
`nodes[0]`'s title and children.

set-split-ratio.name: SetSplitRatioRequest
doc: Divider drag. Reuse one `transaction` per gesture so undo coalesces.
Clamped by the daemon to 0.05...0.95.

move-column.name: MoveColumnRequest
doc: Moves the whole viewport column holding `pane` (every pane, split and
row in it) one place left or right (`column-move-v1`). The daemon refuses
a column at the strip's edge or next to a docked column
(`column-move-edge`) and a docked column (`column-move-docked`).
Any pane of the column that moves.

set-divider-visible.name: SetDividerVisibleRequest
doc: A split's divider drawn or not (`split-divider-visibility-v1`): a hidden divider draws no line
and still drags. The daemon keeps it on the split node, so it persists with the layout.

set-viewport-pane-width.name: SetColumnWidthRequest
doc: Column width drag (`viewport-column-resize-v1`).
0.1...1.0 of the viewport.

set-row-heights.name: SetRowHeightsRequest
doc: `set-row-heights` (`rows-v1`): every row of one column at once. `fit`
requires a sum of exactly 1000.

create-browser-profile.name: CreateBrowserProfileRequest
doc: `create-browser-profile`: an existing id returns the stored record.

pin-workspace.name: PinWorkspaceRequest
doc: Pins a workspace to one room (Move Workspace to Room), replacing any pin.
Caller-chosen id makes a retry idempotent; nil lets the daemon mint one.

move-profile.name: MoveProfileRequest
doc: Moves a profile to an insertion index (the `move-workspace` rule).

update-browser-profile.name: UpdateBrowserProfileRequest
doc: `update-browser-profile`: absent keeps, `.clear` sends null.
The profile's own proxy (#24432), as `cmux browser profile proxy set|clear` sends it; the daemon validates it.

set-personal-workspace.name: SetPersonalWorkspaceRequest
doc: Sets a qualified workspace's personal order (insertion index), group,
browser profile or theme; JSON null clears.
Needs `personal-remote-localhost-v1` unless unchanged.
Moves the group, and pins its members, to another room.

update-profile.name: UpdateProfileRequest
doc: Renames a profile or sets/clears its appearance or terminal defaults.

put-frontend-projection.name: PutFrontendProjectionRequest
doc: CAS write of an opaque (<= 1 MiB) per-window/profile document.

close-screen-group.name: CloseScreenGroupRequest
doc: Closes every member screen. A saved group keeps its saved record.

add-screens-to-screen-group.name: AddScreensToScreenGroupRequest
doc: Adds screens to a group. `index` is the position inside the group (default: the end).

remove-screens-from-screen-group.name: RemoveScreensFromScreenGroupRequest
doc: Removes screens from their groups; each lands right after its former group.

move-screen-group.name: MoveScreenGroupRequest
doc: Moves a whole group to `index` (the final index of its first screen), or
into `workspace`.
Moves the group into a new workspace created in the same commit.
`screen-group-icon-v1`: sent only when set; `.clear` sends `null`, which removes it.

set-screen-metadata.name: SetScreenMetadataRequest
doc: Shared screen color and icon. A field sent as JSON null clears it; an
omitted field keeps its value.
Palette token `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}` or `#RRGGBB[AA]`; frontends offer the nine group colors.
SF Symbol name or one emoji grapheme.

unsave-tab-group.name: UnsaveTabGroupRequest
doc: Deletes the saved record linked to a live group; the group stays.
The live group (not the saved record id).

delete-saved-tab-group.name: DeleteSavedTabGroupRequest
doc: Deletes a saved record by id; a linked live group stays, unlinked.

reopen-saved-tab-group.name: ReopenSavedTabGroupRequest
doc: Reopens a saved group into `pane`. A still-linked live group is returned
unchanged; otherwise running terminals reattach, others start in their
saved directory, and browsers reopen at their saved URL.

list-saved-tab-groups.name: ListSavedTabGroupsRequest
doc: Every saved record.

save-tab-group.name: SaveTabGroupRequest
doc: Saves a live group. Result: `{group, saved}` (the record id).

list-tab-groups.name: ListTabGroupsRequest
doc: Every live group with its pane, in the `Pane.tab_groups` shape.

move-tab-group-to-split.name: MoveTabGroupToSplitRequest
doc: Drops a whole group on a pane edge.

move-tab-group-to-new-workspace.name: MoveTabGroupToNewWorkspaceRequest
doc: Drops a whole group on the sidebar: a new workspace holding the group,
optionally in a sidebar group at a section index. Tear-off = this + open
the returned workspace in a new window.
Sidebar (workspace) group for the new workspace.

remove-tabs-from-tab-group.name: RemoveTabsFromGroupRequest
doc: Removes tabs from their groups; each lands just after its former group.
A group left without members disappears.

surfaces.name: tabs
doc: Wire `surfaces`.

move-tab-group.name: MoveTabGroupRequest
doc: Reorders a group in its strip or moves it into another pane at `index`.

move-tab.name: MoveTabRequest
doc: Reorder within a strip or move into any pane (across screens and
workspaces). Pinned tabs stay first (`tab-metadata-v1`).
Echoed in `tab-changed` (`tab-drag-v1`); 1-128 printable ASCII.

move-tab-to-new-workspace.name: MoveTabToNewWorkspaceRequest
doc: Drop on the sidebar: new workspace holding the tab, optionally in a group
at a final section index. Tear-off = this + open the workspace in a new window.
The new workspace's name (`tab-workspace-name-v1`); nil keeps the
daemon's default. Sent only to a daemon that advertises it.

move-tab-to-workspace.name: MoveTabToWorkspaceRequest
doc: Move into an existing workspace's active pane, or a new workspace when
`workspace` is nil (`tab-workspace-move-v1`).

move-tab-to-split.name: MoveTabToSplitRespawnRequest
doc: `move-tab-to-split` with `respawn`: one owner op that moves the tab into
a new pane beside its own pane and spawns `respawn` in the pane it left.
It can launch a terminal host, so it uses the spawn deadline.

rename-surface.name: RenameTabRequest
doc: Renames a tab. Empty name clears it.

close-pane.name: ClosePaneRequest
doc: `endTerminals` (`batch-close-v1`) also ends, in the same commit, each
terminal whose tabs all close and that is not kept. Sent only when true.

close-screen.name: CloseScreenRequest
doc: `endTerminals` as in `ClosePaneRequest`.

close-tabs.name: CloseTabsRequest
doc: Closes several tabs in one daemon commit (`batch-close-v1`). With
`endTerminals`, each terminal whose tabs all close ends in that same
commit, unless it is kept; a terminal still shown elsewhere keeps running.
Why the tabs close (`close-reason-v1`); `.sessionEnd` keeps them out of closed history.

close-terminal.name: CloseTerminalRequest
doc: Kills the PTY at once. Closing a tab/pane/screen only detaches it; with
`terminal-reap-v1` the daemon ends it after the reap grace period unless kept.

set-frontend-browser-history.name: SetFrontendBrowserHistoryRequest
doc: Stores (or with nil, clears) a frontend browser tab's session history.

set-client-sizing.name: SetClientSizingRequest
doc: Claims (`enabled && exclusive`) or releases canonical geometry.

list-terminals.name: ListTerminalsRequest
doc: `list-terminals`: every terminal in the daemon's registry with its
workspace and, once ended, its exit record (cmux-tui terminal-host.md).

get-blob.name: GetBlobRequest
doc: `get-blob`: `blob` is `blob:sha256-<hex>` or an asset icon value.
`workspace-first-tab-v1`: the workspace's first tab, made by this request; the reply names it
(``WorkspaceMutationResult/firstTab``). Send it only to a daemon that serves the capability.

set-workspace-metadata.name: SetWorkspaceMetadataRequest
doc: Shared color/icon/title (`workspace-metadata-v1`), the sidebar pin
(`workspace-pin-v1`), and the manual unread mark
(`notification-mark-unread-v1`). Emits `workspace-changed`.
Palette token `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}` or `#RRGGBB[AA]`.
SF Symbol name.
1-256 characters; overrides `name` for display.
Nil leaves the pin unchanged; the field has no clear state.
Nil leaves the manual unread mark unchanged.

new-pane.name: NewPaneRequest
doc: Adds a pane to the pane's column (vertical stack inside a column).

page-credential.name: ScopedPageCredentialRequest
doc: `page-credential {page}` (`page-credential-scoped-v1`): a single-use credential bound to one
page of the daemon's page-router table, for any trusted local connection. It admits only a
WebSocket handshake whose Origin names that page and never carries the person's Cloud lease,
so it is narrower than the file token next to the socket.
The page id (`home-channels`).

remote-host-status.name: RemoteHostStatusRequest
doc: `remote-host-status` (`remote-host-v1`, docs/cmux-remote.md): cmux Remote's state as the
daemon sees it (never starts the host).

remote-host-call.name: RemoteHostCallRequest
doc: `remote-host-call {method, params}`: one cmux Remote request (status, refresh, request,
open_settings, restart, screen.share, screen.access, screen.stop_session).

computer-use-config.name: ComputerUseConfigRequest
doc: `computer-use-config {config}`: the person's Computer Use policy (`PolicyConfig` JSON), from this
verified app. On macOS the daemon hands it to cmux Remote's Computer Use worker.

computer-use-approvals.name: ComputerUseApprovalsRequest
doc: `computer-use-approvals {action, app_id?}`: list, forget, always, never or revoke_sessions.
